title: First recording date with Billie Holiday and Lester Young
summary: Days later he arrived first at the studio and recorded with Billie, Teddy Wilson, Lester, Buck Clayton and Jo Jones.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And, I think the next day, or two days later, or something like that I had a recording date. You know, they said "Why don't you go down to the studio" -- some studio -- I forgot what studio.
Decca they were recording with, weren't they?
You mean the things with Billy? Billie
Huh? The things with Billy? Yeah.
Oh, I though you meant that Basie.
And, I walked in. I was the first one there, you know (laugh).
And, I walked in, and I think they were setting up the mikes, and what-not. And, then in walks -- I think Pres walked in first, and then Buck walked in, you know. And then came Benny.
And, then, you know, I realized I was all alone -- (laugh).
And then Lady walked in. And I thought 'Wow'.
Oh, listen -- yeah. And, you know, Teddy and, -- oh, listen -- then Jo Jones and -- we got on with it.
Well, did those guys act like they recognized you?
Yeah. They recognized, you know. They came over to me and said hello.
Well, you've got to realize that they themselves were -- I mean, after all, the Basie band was --
Yeah. They were kind of nervous, too.
Yeah. You know -- here in a big city, you know what I mean?
But, we got along. We got along alright.
Was that the first time you'd ever heard Billy?
You'd heard her at other clubs -- you'd heard her uptown?
No. I think I'd heard her before. I heard her -- I think I heard her uptown, somewhere. I don't remember where, but I'm sure I heard her before that. Had to, heard about her.

Yeah. So, we got along with it -- the recording thing -- which you know, I -- it was really to me it was easy. I expected it to be a really hard thing, you know. But, then we walked in, and Billy would walk in was working with her music, you know. Nothing written out, just a piano copy. Songs she'd put on the top of the piano, and Teddy would run over it. And we would go on with it.
Yeah. Teddy -- that's right. "You've got this and you've got that". And, we taped the first chorus and Lester would come in on it, and that's --
And it worked out. No problems?
And, you wouldn't have to do that many takes, either?
No, no. No, we didn't do many takes on it.
Well, I should think that was one of the big musical thrills of your life, wasn't it?
Oh, that was. That was tops.
Well, obviously we've got to talk quite a bit about Walter Page.
